verses.1:1: The word of the Lord, which came to Hosea, son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.1:2: The beginning of the Lord's speaking in Hosea. And the Lord said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of fornications, and have for yourself children of fornications, because the land, committing fornication, will commit fornication away from the Lord."
verses.1:3: And he departed and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.1:4: And the Lord said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, because yet a little while, and I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease.
verses.1:5: And on that day I will shatter the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel."
verses.1:6: And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And He said to him, "Call her name Without Mercy, because I will no longer continue to have mercy on the house of Israel, but in forgetfulness I will forget them.
verses.1:7: And on the house of Judah I will have mercy, and I will save them by the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow and sword, or by war, or by horses, or by horsemen."
verses.1:8: And she weaned her who was Without Mercy. And she conceived and bore a son.
verses.1:9: And He said, "Call his name Not My People, because you are not My people, and I will not be yours."
verses.2:1: And the number of the sons of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which is without measure and will not be numbered. And it will be, in the place where it will be said to them, "You are not My people," that it will be said to them, "Sons of the living God."
verses.2:2: And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be assembled together; and they will appoint for themselves one head, and they will go up from the land, because great is the day of Jezreel.
verses.2:3: Say to your brothers, "My People," and to your sister, "Having Obtained Mercy."
verses.2:4: Judge your mother, judge, because she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
verses.2:5: or else I will strip her naked, and set her as on the day of her birth, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a trackless land, and kill her with thirst.
verses.2:6: And I will not have mercy on her children, because they are children of fornications.
verses.2:7: For their mother has committed fornication; she who conceived them has been put to shame, for she said, "I will go after my lovers, who give bread to me, and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
verses.2:8: For this reason, look, I will fence in your way with thorns, and I will fence it in with a stone wall, and she will not find her paths.
verses.2:9: And she will pursue her lovers, and will not overtake them; and she will seek them, and will not find them; and she will say, "I will go and return to my former husband, because it was better for me then than now."
verses.2:10: And she did not know that I gave her grain, and wine, and oil, and multiplied silver for her, and gold, which they made for Baal.
verses.2:11: Therefore I will turn back and take My grain in its time, and My wine in its time. And I will rescue My wool and My flax, which covered her disgrace.
verses.2:12: And now I will uncover her folly before the eyes of her lovers, and no man will snatch her from My hand;
verses.2:13: and I will cause all her joy to cease, her festival, her new moon, her Sabbath, and all her festive times.
verses.2:14: And I will ruin her vineyard and her fig tree, about which she said, "These are my wages, which my lovers have given me"; and I will turn it into a forest, and the beast of the field will devour it.
verses.2:15: And I will visit upon her the days of the Baals, on which she burned incense, and adorned herself with her earring and her necklace. And she went after her lovers, and forgot Me, says the Lord.
verses.2:16: For this reason, look, I will allure her, and lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
verses.2:17: And I will give her vinedressers to her from that same place, and the valley of Achor to open hope; and she will sing there as in the days of her youth, and as in the days of her ascent from the land of Egypt.
verses.2:18: And it will be on that day, says the Lord: she will call Me "My husband," and she will no longer call Me "Baali."
verses.2:19: And I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and she will no longer remember their name.
verses.2:20: And I will make a covenant with them on that day, with the beast of the field, and with the bird of the sky, and with the creeping thing of the earth; and I will shatter bow, and sword, and war from the earth, and I will make them sleep with confidence.
verses.2:21: And I will betroth you to Myself forever; and I will betroth you to Myself in righteousness and justice, and in mercy, and in compassions.
verses.2:22: And I will betroth you to Myself in faithfulness; and you will know that I am the Lord.
verses.2:23: And it will be on that day: I will hear, says the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they will hear the earth.
verses.2:24: And the earth will hear the wheat, and the wine, and the oil, and these will hear Jezreel.
verses.2:25: And I will sow her for Myself in the earth, and I will have mercy on her who was Without Mercy.
verses.3:1: And the Lord said to me, "Go again, and love a woman who is loved by a friend and is an adulteress, just as the Lord loves the sons of Israel, though they themselves look to foreign gods and love the husks of grapes."
verses.3:2: And I dug her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a cor of barley, and half a cor of barley.
verses.3:3: And I said to her, "For many days you will wait for me; you will not commit fornication, and you will not belong to a man; yet I also will wait for you."
verses.3:4: Because for many days the sons of Israel will sit without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an altar, and without an ephod, and without teraphim.
verses.3:5: And after these things the sons of Israel will return, and they will seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and they will tremble before the Lord and before His goodness in the last days.
verses.4:1: Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, because the Lord has a legal dispute with the inhabitants of the land; for there is no truth, nor is there mercy, nor is there knowledge of God in the land.
verses.4:2: Cursing, falsehood, murder, theft, and adultery have overflowed, and blood has touched blood.
verses.4:3: Because of this, the land will mourn, and everyone who lives in it will grow weak, together with the beast of the field and the bird of the sky; and even the fish of the sea will be gathered together.
verses.4:4: Yet let no one judge, and let no man be reproved; for your people are like those who oppose the priest.
verses.4:5: And you will fall down today, and the prophet will also fall down with you. At night I have caused your mother to be silent.
verses.4:6: My people have fallen silent because they had no knowledge. Since you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you so that you may not exercise the priesthood for Me. And you have forgotten the law of your God; I too will forget your children.
verses.4:7: According to their multitude, so they have sinned against Me; I will exchange their glory for disgrace.
verses.4:8: They will eat the sins of My people, and toward their iniquity they will lift up their souls.
verses.4:9: And it will be: like the people, so the priest; and I will call him to account for his ways, and I will repay his thoughts to him.
verses.4:10: And they will eat and not be satisfied; they have committed fornication and have not ceased, because they have abandoned the Lord by not taking heed.
verses.4:11: Fornication, wine, and drunkenness take away the heart.
verses.4:12: My people have inquired of their wood, and their staff has told them; for a spirit of fornications has deceived them, and they have committed fornication away from their God.
verses.4:13: Upon the tops of the mountains they were sacrificing, and upon the hills they were sending up incense, beneath an oak, a poplar, and a terebinth, because its shade was good; therefore your daughters will commit fornication, and your brides will be adulteresses.
verses.4:14: I will not call your daughters to account when they have committed fornication, nor your brides when they have committed adultery; for they themselves were consorting with prostitutes and sacrificing with effeminate men, and a people without understanding will be beaten.
verses.4:15: If you commit fornication, Israel, at least let Judah not become guilty; and do not enter Gilgal, and do not go up to Beth-aven, nor swear, "The Lord lives!"
verses.4:16: For like an unruly cow, Israel has turned aside; now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in a wide place.
verses.4:17: Ephraim is a partner of idols; leave him alone.
verses.4:18: Their banquet is separated; in fornication they have committed fornication; his protectors have loved to bring disgrace.
verses.4:19: The wind has bound him in its wings, and they will be put to shame because of their sacrifices.
verses.5:1: Hear this, priests, and pay attention, house of Israel, and house of the king, listen closely; for judgment belongs to you, because you have become a snare to the watch and a net spread out over Tabor.
verses.5:2: And you have turned sacrificial victims aside into the deep, and I am the instructor of them all.
verses.5:3: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me; for now Ephraim has committed fornication; Israel has been defiled.
verses.5:4: They will not give their thoughts so that they may return to their God, because a spirit of fornications is in their midst, and they have not known the Lord.
verses.5:5: And the arrogance of Israel will answer to his face, and Israel and Ephraim will fall in their iniquity; Judah will also fall with them.
verses.5:6: With their flocks and with their herds they will go to seek the Lord, and they will not find Him; He has been taken away from them.
verses.5:7: They have broken faith with the Lord, because they have fathered foreign children; now a month will devour them together with their portions.
verses.5:8: Sound the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; wail in Beth-aven, behind your back, Benjamin.
verses.5:9: Ephraim will be in desolation on the day of rebuke; among the tribes of Israel I have shown faithfulness.
verses.5:10: The princes of Judah have become like those who take up a boundary; upon them I will pour out My anger like water.
verses.5:11: Ephraim is suffering false accusation, broken in judgment, because he began to go away after filth.
verses.5:12: And I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.
verses.5:13: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his bond; and Ephraim went away to Assyria and sent to the avenging king. Yet he himself will not be able to heal you, nor will he be able to untie the bond from you.
verses.5:14: For I am like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a lion cub to the house of Judah. I, I will seize and depart; I will carry off, and there is no one who can rescue.
verses.5:15: Going away, I will return to My place until you grow faint and seek My face.
verses.6:1: In their distress they will rise up early to Me: "Come, and let us return to the Lord.
verses.6:2: He will make us alive after two days; on the third day He will raise us up, and we will live in His presence.
verses.6:3: We will know, and we will follow so that we may know the Lord; His going forth is prepared like the dawn, and He will come to us like rain, early and late, for the earth."
verses.6:4: What am I to do with you, Ephraim? What am I to do with you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like dew passing away early.
verses.6:5: Because of this I have hewn them by the prophets; I have killed them by the words of My mouth, and your judgments will go forth like light.
verses.6:6: Because I have desired mercy and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
verses.6:7: Yet they themselves, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they have broken faith with Me.
verses.6:8: Gilead is a city of those who make an idol, undermined by blood.
verses.6:9: And like the jaws of robber men, it is a partner of priests who kill on the road those traveling from Shechem, because they have committed a wicked crime.
verses.6:10: In the house of Israel I have seen something horrifying: there are the fornications of Ephraim; Israel has been defiled.
verses.6:11: Moreover, Judah, set a harvest for yourself when I turn back the captivity of My people.
verses.7:1: When I wished to heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was revealed, and the wickedness of Samaria, because they have practiced falsehood; and a thief has entered plundering; a bandit is outside.
verses.7:2: And so that they may not perhaps say in their hearts that I have remembered all their wickedness, now their own devices have surrounded them; they have been done before My face.
verses.7:3: In their wickedness they have gladdened the king, and in their falsehoods the princes.
verses.7:4: All of them are committing adultery, like an oven kindled by the baker; the city rested for a little while from the mixing of the leaven, until the whole was leavened.
verses.7:5: The day of our king: the princes began to rage from wine; he stretched out his hand with mockers.
verses.7:6: For they applied their heart like an oven while he was lying in wait for them; all night the one baking them slept; in the morning he himself is kindled like a fire of flame.
verses.7:7: All of them have been heated like an oven, and they have devoured their judges; all their kings have fallen; there is no one among them who cries out to Me.
verses.7:8: Ephraim himself was mingling among the peoples; Ephraim has become ash-baked bread that is not turned over.
verses.7:9: Foreigners have consumed his strength, and he himself did not know it; and even gray hairs have spread upon him, and he himself was unaware of it.
verses.7:10: And the pride of Israel will be humbled to his face; yet they have not returned to the Lord their God, and they have not sought Him in all these things.
verses.7:11: And Ephraim has become like a misled dove having no heart. They were calling upon Egypt; they went away to the Assyrians.
verses.7:12: And when they set out, I will spread My net over them; like a bird of the sky I will bring them down; I will strike them according to the report of their assembly.
verses.7:13: Woe to them, because they have departed from Me! They will be devastated, because they have rebelled against Me; and I redeemed them, yet they themselves have spoken falsehoods against Me.
verses.7:14: And they have not cried out to Me in their heart, but they were wailing on their beds; over wheat and wine they were ruminating; they have departed from Me.
verses.7:15: And I instructed them and strengthened their arms, yet against Me they devised wickedness.
verses.7:16: They turned back so that they might be without a yoke; they have become like a deceitful bow; their princes will fall by the sword from the rage of their tongue. This is their derision in the land of Egypt.
verses.8:1: Let a trumpet be in your throat, like an eagle over the house of the Lord, because they have transgressed My covenant and have rebelled against My law.
verses.8:2: They will call upon Me: "My God, we Israel have known You."
verses.8:3: Israel has cast off what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
verses.8:4: They themselves have reigned, and not from Me; they have become princes, and I did not know it; their silver and their gold they have made into idols for themselves, so that they might perish.
verses.8:5: Your calf has been cast off, Samaria; My fury is incensed against them. How long will they be unable to be cleansed?
verses.8:6: For it too is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not a god; for the calf of Samaria will become spiders' webs.
verses.8:7: Because they will sow wind, and they will harvest a whirlwind; there is no standing stalk in it; the shoot will not produce flour; and even if it does produce it, foreigners will eat it.
verses.8:8: Israel has been devoured; now he has become among the nations like an unclean vessel.
verses.8:9: For they themselves have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey solitary by itself; Ephraim has given gifts to lovers.
verses.8:10: Yet even when they have hired the nations for wages, now I will gather them, and they will rest for a little while from the burden of the king and of the princes.
verses.8:11: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, altars have become an offense to him.
verses.8:12: I will write for him My manifold laws, which have been counted as foreign.
verses.8:13: They will offer sacrifices, they will slaughter meat and eat, and the Lord will not accept them; now He will remember their iniquity and will punish their sins; they themselves will turn back to Egypt.
verses.8:14: And Israel has forgotten his Maker and has built shrines, and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; and I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour his palaces.
verses.9:1: Do not rejoice, Israel; do not exult like the peoples; for you have committed fornication away from your God; you have loved wages on all the threshing floors of wheat.
verses.9:2: The threshing floor and the winepress will not feed them, and the wine will lie to them.
verses.9:3: They will not dwell in the land of the Lord. Ephraim has returned to Egypt, and among the Assyrians he has eaten what is polluted.
verses.9:4: They will not pour out wine as a libation to the Lord, and they will not be pleasing to Him. Their sacrifices are like the bread of mourners; all who eat it will be defiled; for their bread is for their own soul; it will not enter into the house of the Lord.
verses.9:5: What will you do on the solemn day, on the day of the festival of the Lord?
verses.9:6: For look, they have set out from devastation: Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them; the nettle will inherit their desirable silver; burdock will be in their tents.
verses.9:7: The days of visitation have come; the days of retribution have come. Know, Israel, that the prophet is foolish, the spiritual man is mad, because of the multitude of your iniquity and the multitude of madness.
verses.9:8: The watchman of Ephraim is with my God; the prophet has become a snare of ruin on all his ways; insanity is in the house of his God.
verses.9:9: They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their iniquity and will punish their sins.
verses.9:10: Like grapes in the desert I found Israel; like the first fruits of the fig tree at its top I saw their fathers; but they themselves went in to Baal-peor, and alienated themselves to shame, and became abominable like the things that they loved.
verses.9:11: Ephraim has flown away like a bird; their glory, from birth, and from the womb, and from conception.
verses.9:12: And even if they bring up their sons, I will make them childless among men; moreover, woe to them when I depart from them!
verses.9:13: Ephraim, as I saw, was Tyre, founded in beauty; and Ephraim will lead out his sons to the killer.
verses.9:14: Give them, Lord. What will You give them? Give them a womb without children and dry breasts.
verses.9:15: All their evils are in Gilgal, for there I held them in hatred. Because of the wickedness of their devices, I will drive them out of My house; I will not continue to love them; all their princes are turning away.
verses.9:16: Ephraim has been struck; their root has dried up; they will by no means produce fruit; and even if they give birth, I will kill the most beloved ones of their womb.
verses.9:17: My God will cast them away, because they have not listened to Him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.
verses.10:1: Israel is a leafy vine; the fruit was matched to it. According to the abundance of its fruit it multiplied altars; according to the fertility of its land it abounded in images.
verses.10:2: Their heart is divided; now they will perish. He Himself will shatter their images; He will lay waste their altars.
verses.10:3: For now they will say, "There is no king for us, for we do not fear the Lord; and what will a king do for us?"
verses.10:4: You speak words of a worthless vision, and you will strike a covenant; and judgment will sprout like bitterness upon the furrows of the field.
verses.10:5: The inhabitants of Samaria worshiped the cows of Beth-aven; for its people mourned over it, and its temple attendants exulted over it in its glory, because it has departed from it.
verses.10:6: For indeed it itself has been carried off to Assyria, a gift to the avenging king. Shame will seize Ephraim, and Israel will be put to shame in its own will.
verses.10:7: Samaria has caused her king to pass away like foam upon the face of the water.
verses.10:8: And the high places of the idol, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed; burdock and thistle will come up upon their altars, and they will say to the mountains, "Cover us," and to the hills, "Fall upon us."
verses.10:9: From the days of Gibeah Israel has sinned; there they stood. Battle against the sons of iniquity will not overtake them in Gibeah.
verses.10:10: According to My desire I will chastise them; peoples will be gathered against them when they are chastised for their two iniquities.
verses.10:11: Ephraim is a heifer taught to love threshing, and I passed over the beauty of her neck; I will ride upon Ephraim, Judah will plow, Jacob will break up the furrows for himself.
verses.10:12: Sow for yourselves in righteousness, and reap in the mouth of mercy. Renew for yourselves fallow ground; and it is time to seek the Lord, when He comes who will teach you righteousness.
verses.10:13: You have plowed ungodliness, you have reaped iniquity; you have eaten the fruit of falsehood, because you have trusted in your ways, in the multitude of your mighty men.
verses.10:14: An uproar will rise up among your people, and all your fortresses will be laid waste, just as Salmana was laid waste by the house of him who judged Baal in the day of battle, with the mother dashed to pieces upon the children.
verses.10:15: Thus has Bethel done to you, because of the malice of your wicked deeds.
verses.11:1: As the morning has passed, the king of Israel has passed away. For Israel was a child, and I loved him, and from Egypt I called My son.
verses.11:2: They called them; thus they went away from their presence. They made offerings to the Baals, and they sacrificed to images.
verses.11:3: And I was like a nurturer to Ephraim; I carried them in My arms, and they did not know that I cared for them.
verses.11:4: With the cords of Adam I will draw them, with the bonds of love; and I will be to them like one lifting up the yoke over their jaws, and I bent down to him so that he might eat.
verses.11:5: He will not return to the land of Egypt, and Assyria itself will be his king, because they refused to turn back.
verses.11:6: The sword has begun in his cities, and it will consume his chosen ones, and will devour their heads.
verses.11:7: And My people will hang in suspense for My return; but a yoke will be laid upon them all together, which will not be taken away.
verses.11:8: How shall I give you up, Ephraim? Shall I protect you, Israel? How shall I make you like Admah, set you like Zeboiim? My heart has turned within Me; at the same time My repentance is deeply troubled.
verses.11:9: I will not execute the fury of My anger; I will not turn back to destroy Ephraim, for I am God, and not man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter the city.
verses.11:10: They will walk after the Lord; He will roar like a lion, for He Himself will roar, and the sons of the sea will be afraid.
verses.11:11: And they will fly away like a bird from Egypt, and like a dove from the land of the Assyrians; and I will settle them in their houses, says the Lord.
verses.12:1: Ephraim has surrounded Me with denial, and the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah went down as a witness with God, and is faithful with the holy ones.
verses.12:2: Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the scorching heat; all day long he multiplies falsehood and devastation, and he entered into a covenant with the Assyrians and was carrying oil to Egypt.
verses.12:3: Therefore the judgment of the Lord is with Judah, and a visitation upon Jacob; according to his ways and according to his schemes He will repay him.
verses.12:4: In the womb he supplanted his brother, and in his strength he was directed with an angel.
verses.12:5: And he prevailed against the angel and was strengthened; he wept and pleaded with him. In Bethel He found him, and there He spoke with us.
verses.12:6: And the Lord God of hosts, the Lord is His memorial.
verses.12:7: And you will turn back to your God; keep mercy and justice, and hope in your God always.
verses.12:8: Canaan, in his hand is a deceitful balance; he has loved extortion.
verses.12:9: And Ephraim said, "Indeed I have become rich; I have found an idol for myself. All my labors will not find in me iniquity that I have sinned."
verses.12:10: And I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt; I will yet make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the festival.
verses.12:11: And I spoke to the prophets, and I multiplied vision, and by the hand of the prophets I was likened.
verses.12:12: If Gilead is an idol, then in vain were they sacrificing bulls in Gilgal; for even their altars are like heaps upon the furrows of the field.
verses.12:13: Jacob fled into the region of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept watch.
verses.12:14: And by a prophet the Lord led Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was kept.
verses.12:15: Ephraim has provoked Me to anger in his bitternesses; and his blood will come upon him, and his Lord will return his reproach to him.
verses.13:1: When Ephraim spoke, dread fell upon Israel; and he transgressed in Baal, and died.
verses.13:2: And now they have continued to sin; and they have made for themselves a cast image from their silver as a likeness of idols; all of it is the handiwork of craftsmen. To these they themselves say, "Sacrifice human beings, you who worship calves."
verses.13:3: Therefore they will be like a morning cloud, and like morning dew passing away; like dust snatched by a whirlwind from the threshing floor, and like smoke from a chimney.
verses.13:4: But I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt; and you will know no God apart from Me, and there is no savior except Me.
verses.13:5: I knew you in the desert, in a land of solitude.
verses.13:6: According to their pastures they were filled and were satisfied; and they lifted up their heart, and they forgot Me.
verses.13:7: And I will be to them like a lioness, like a leopard on the road of the Assyrians.
verses.13:8: I will meet them like a bear whose cubs have been snatched away, and I will rip open the inner parts of their liver, and I will devour them there like a lion; the beast of the field will tear them apart.
verses.13:9: Destruction is yours, Israel; only in Me is your help.
verses.13:10: Where is your king? Especially now let him save you in all your cities; and your judges, about whom you said, "Give me a king and princes."
verses.13:11: I will give you a king in My fury, and I will take him away in My indignation.
verses.13:12: Ephraim's iniquity is bound up; his sin is concealed.
verses.13:13: The pains of a woman in labor will come upon him; he himself is not a wise son, for now he will not stand in the crushing of children.
verses.13:14: From the hand of death I will deliver them; from death I will redeem them. I will be your death, death! Your bite I will be, underworld! Consolation is concealed from My eyes.
verses.13:15: Because he himself will divide among brothers, the Lord will bring a burning wind rising from the desert, and He will dry up his springs and lay waste his fountain; and He Himself will plunder the treasury of every desirable vessel.
verses.14:1: May Samaria perish, because she has provoked her God to bitterness! By the sword let them perish, let their little children be dashed to pieces, and let her pregnant women be torn open!
verses.14:2: Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, because you have fallen in your iniquity.
verses.14:3: Take words with you, and return to the Lord; and say to Him, "Take away all iniquity, accept what is good, and we will offer the calves of our lips.
verses.14:4: Assyria will not save us; we will not mount a horse, nor will we say any longer, 'Our gods are the works of our hands,' because You will have mercy on the orphan who is in You."
verses.14:5: I will heal their bruises; I will love them freely, because My fury has turned away from them.
verses.14:6: I will be like dew; Israel will sprout like a lily, and his root will burst forth like that of Lebanon.
verses.14:7: His branches will go forth, and his glory will be like an olive tree, and his fragrance like that of Lebanon.
verses.14:8: Those who sit in his shadow will return; they will live on wheat, and they will sprout like a vine; his memorial will be like the wine of Lebanon.
verses.14:9: Ephraim, what are idols to Me any longer? I will hear, and I Myself will direct him like a green fir tree; from Me your fruit has been found.
verses.14:10: Who is wise, and will understand those things? Who is discerning, and will know these things? For the ways of the Lord are straight, and the righteous will walk in them; but transgressors will fall in them.

notes.1:2: Latin "Principium loquendi Domino in Osee" ("the Lord's speaking in Hosea") literally preserves the preposition "in" (speaking within or through the prophet), and "committing fornication, will commit fornication" keeps the Vulgate's emphatic participle-and-verb construction.
notes.1:4: Latin "visitabo ... super" ("I will visit ... upon") is a literal Vulgate idiom for calling to account or punishing (cf. 2:15).
notes.1:6: The Vulgate translates the children's symbolic names into Latin ("Absque misericordia", "Without Mercy"; "Non populus meus", "Not My People" in 1:9) rather than transliterating the Hebrew. Its closing clause "oblivione obliviscar eorum" ("in forgetfulness I will forget them") is a distinctly Vulgate reading where the Hebrew is read as refusing forgiveness or as carrying away.
notes.2:1: As in the Hebrew, chapter 2 begins here; in the other common versification, 2:1-2 are numbered 1:10-11, and 2:3-25 are 2:1-23. The Vulgate also leaves "Filii Dei viventis" ("Sons of the living God") concise without an explicit verb.
notes.2:11: Latin "liberabo" literally means "I will rescue" or "deliver," preserving the vivid metaphor of snatching His gifts away; "ignominiam" ("disgrace") renders the Hebrew "nakedness," just as "stultitiam" ("folly") renders "lewdness" in 2:12.
notes.2:17: Distinctly Vulgate readings here include "vinitores ejus" ("her vinedressers," where the Hebrew reads "her vineyards"), "ad aperiendam spem" ("to open hope," vs. Hebrew "a door of hope"), and "canet" ("she will sing").
notes.2:18: Where the Hebrew uses second person ("you will call"), the Vulgate reads third person ("vocabit", "she will call," continuing in 2:19 with "she will no longer remember"). "Baali" means "my master" or "my Baal," contrasting with "My husband."
notes.2:25: In 2:23-24, Latin "exaudiam" ("I will hear" favorably) renders the Hebrew "answer." This Latin text concludes chapter 2 after "Without Mercy," without the additional clause addressing "Not My People" found in the Hebrew and some Latin witnesses.
notes.3:1: Latin "vinacia uvarum" ("the husks of grapes," i.e., pressed grape skins and seeds) is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew has "raisin cakes."
notes.3:2: Latin "fodi" ("I dug") translates the Hebrew verb via its homonym "dig/pierce" (which Jerome linked to piercing a servant's ear in Exodus 21:6) rather than "buy"; "a cor ... and half a cor" renders the Hebrew homer and lethech.
notes.3:3: The Vulgate uses "exspectabis ... exspectabo" ("you will wait for ... I will wait for") symmetrically at the opening and close of Hosea's speech.
notes.3:4: Latin "altari" ("an altar") follows the Septuagint tradition where the Hebrew reads "sacred pillar."
notes.4:3: The Vulgate renders the closing verb literally as congregabuntur ("will be gathered together"), reflecting the primary sense of the Hebrew root for gathering rather than "be swept away."
notes.4:5: Unlike the Hebrew division (which attaches "by night" to the prophet's stumbling and reads "I will destroy your mother"), the Vulgate opens a new sentence with Nocte ("At night") and renders tacere feci ("I have caused to be silent"), connecting directly to Conticuit ("have fallen silent") in 4:6.
notes.4:10: The Vulgate reads et non cessaverunt ("and have not ceased") rather than the Hebrew "and will not increase," and translates the closing phrase literally with the gerund in non custodiendo ("by not taking heed").
notes.4:14: The Vulgate translates cum effeminatis ("with effeminate men") where the Hebrew has feminine cult prostitutes, and renders the closing verb concretely as vapulabit ("will be beaten").
notes.4:18: The Vulgate translates the opening clause as Separatum est convivium eorum ("Their banquet is separated") rather than "Their drinking is gone," and renders the difficult closing words as dilexerunt afferre ignominiam protectores ejus ("his protectors have loved to bring disgrace").
notes.5:1: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Mizpah etymologically as a common noun, speculationi ("to the watch" or "lookout").
notes.5:2: Where the Hebrew is obscure ("the revolters have gone deep in slaughter"), the Vulgate reads victimas declinastis in profundum ("you have turned sacrificial victims aside into the deep") and renders the closing noun as an agent, eruditor ("instructor").
notes.5:4: The Vulgate takes cogitationes suas ("their thoughts") as the direct object of Non dabunt ("They will not give"), rather than making "their deeds" the subject as in the Hebrew text.
notes.5:13: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew for "wound" twice as vinculum ("bond"), and translates Hebrew "King Jareb" (or "the great king") etymologically as regem ultorem ("the avenging king").
notes.5:15: The Vulgate uses second-person plural verbs and translates deficiatis ("until you grow faint") where the Hebrew has third-person plural "until they acknowledge their guilt."
notes.6:1: In Vulgate verse numbering, the opening clause ("In their distress they will rise up early to Me") begins chapter 6 rather than closing 5:15 as in the Hebrew text.
notes.6:5: The Vulgate has plural judicia tua ("your judgments"), as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, where the Septuagint reads singular "my judgment."
notes.6:7: The Vulgate reads sicut Adam ("like Adam") as a reference to the first man, whereas the Hebrew phrase can also be taken as "like mankind" or "at Adam."
notes.6:8: The Vulgate renders operantium idolum ("those who make an idol") rather than "workers of iniquity," and translates the Hebrew root for "heel" as supplantata ("undermined" or "tripped up").
notes.6:9: The Vulgate translates the difficult opening phrase as fauces ("jaws") and reads de Sichem ("from Shechem," rather than "toward Shechem"), with particeps ("a partner") continuing the description of Gilead from 6:8.
notes.7:2: Vulgate reads "ne forte dicant" ("so that they may not perhaps say"), rendering the Hebrew negation as a negative purpose clause rather than a simple statement ("they do not consider").
notes.7:4: Vulgate uniquely reads "civitas" ("the city"), taking the Hebrew word otherwise read as "from stirring [the fire]" as "the city."
notes.7:10: Vulgate reads "humiliabitur" ("will be humbled"), following the Septuagint in deriving the Hebrew verb from the root meaning "to humble" rather than "to testify."
notes.7:14: Vulgate renders the debated Hebrew verb ("gather together" or "gash themselves") as "ruminabant" ("they were ruminating," literally chewing the cud or brooding over).
notes.7:16: Vulgate reads "ut essent absque jugo" ("so that they might be without a yoke"), understanding the Hebrew consonantal text as "without a yoke" rather than "not upward" or "not to the Most High."
notes.8:4: Vulgate renders the verbs intransitively ("They themselves have reigned... they have become princes") rather than causatively as in the Hebrew ("they set up kings... they appointed princes").
notes.8:6: Vulgate reads "in aranearum telas" ("spiders' webs") for a rare Hebrew term generally taken to mean "splinters" or "broken pieces."
notes.8:10: Vulgate reads "quiescent paulisper" ("they will rest for a little while," agreeing with the Septuagint) and coordinates "regis et principum" ("of the king and of the princes") where the Hebrew has "the king of princes."
notes.8:13: Latin "visitabit" literally means "will visit" in the biblical sense of judicial inspection and punishment (recurring in 9:9 and linked to "visitation" in 9:7).
notes.9:7: Vulgate reads "amentiæ" ("madness") here and "insania" ("insanity") in 9:8 for a Hebrew noun meaning "hostility" or "enmity."
notes.9:8: Vulgate renders the Hebrew "fowler's snare" as "laqueus ruinæ" ("a snare of ruin") and makes "propheta" ("the prophet") the subject of that clause.
notes.9:10: Vulgate reads "in cacumine ejus" ("at its top"), taking the Hebrew term for "in its first season" in a spatial sense.
notes.9:11: Following the Clementine Vulgate punctuation and past tense "avolavit," the verb "has flown away" carries over by ellipsis to "their glory" in the second clause.
notes.9:13: Vulgate reads "Tyrus erat fundata in pulchritudine" ("was Tyre, founded in beauty"), presenting the comparison to Tyre as a direct metaphor and rendering Hebrew "meadow" or "pleasant place" as "beauty."
notes.10:4: The Vulgate reads visionis inutilis ("a worthless vision") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "false oaths."
notes.10:5: The Vulgate renders the verbs as coluerunt ("worshiped") and exsultaverunt ("exulted"), whereas the Hebrew text is commonly read as trembling and wailing over the calf of Beth-aven.
notes.10:6: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew title melekh yarev ("the great king" or "King Jareb") as regi ultori ("the avenging king").
notes.10:12: "In the mouth of mercy" (in ore misericordiae) is a literal Vulgate rendering of the Hebrew idiom meaning "according to mercy," and "who will teach you righteousness" reflects the Vulgate reading of the Hebrew verb yoreh as "teach" rather than "rain."
notes.10:14: A distinctively Vulgate reading: Salmana (the Latin form of Zalmunna) and "the house of him who judged Baal" (alluding to Gideon/Jerubbaal) correspond to "Shalman" and "Beth-arbel" in the Hebrew text.
notes.11:1: In the Clementine Vulgate, the opening sentence ("As the morning has passed, the king of Israel has passed away") begins 11:1 rather than closing 10:15 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:4: The Vulgate retains Adam as a proper name for Hebrew adam ("human" or "man") and uses future tenses ("I will draw," "I will be") before shifting to the past ("I bent down").
notes.11:6: The Vulgate reads Coepit ("has begun"), electos ejus ("his chosen ones"), and capita eorum ("their heads"), where the Hebrew text speaks of the sword whirling, consuming bars or oracle-priests, and devouring because of their counsels.
notes.11:7: A distinctively Vulgate reading ("hang in suspense for My return; but a yoke will be laid upon them") where the Hebrew text speaks of the people being bent on turning away and calling to the Most High.
notes.11:8: The Vulgate translates the second question as protegam te ("Shall I protect you?"), understanding the Hebrew verb from the root for "shield" rather than "hand over."
notes.12:1: The Vulgate reads testis descendit ("went down as a witness") where the Hebrew text reads "still rules" or "is unruly."
notes.12:4: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "strove with God" as directus est cum angelo ("was directed with an angel," also understood in Vulgate usage as "succeeded with an angel").
notes.12:8: The Vulgate preserves Chanaan ("Canaan") as a proper name; in Hebrew the same word can also mean "merchant."
notes.12:9: The Vulgate reads idolum ("an idol") for Hebrew on ("wealth"), connecting it with aven ("idolatry" or "wickedness"), as also in 10:8 and 12:12.
notes.12:11: The Vulgate translates assimilatus sum passively ("I was likened," that is, represented through prophetic likenesses), whereas the Hebrew verb is active ("I gave parables").
notes.13:2: Vulgate "quasi similitudinem idolorum" ("as a likeness of idols") and the imperative "Immolate homines, vitulos adorantes" ("Sacrifice human beings, you who worship calves") reflect distinctly Vulgate readings compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("according to their skill, idols ... men who sacrifice kiss calves").
notes.13:7: Vulgate "in via Assyriorum" ("on the road of the Assyrians") takes the final Hebrew word as the nation Assyria, matching the Septuagint, whereas the Masoretic Text reads it as a verb ("I will watch/lurk").
notes.13:13: Vulgate "in contritione filiorum" ("in the crushing of children") renders the Hebrew childbirth term ("opening of the womb") literally through its root meaning "break" or "crush."
notes.13:14: Vulgate renders the central lines as affirmative declarations ("I will be your death ... Your bite I will be") rather than the questions of the Masoretic Text ("Where are your plagues ...?"), and reads "of death" ("mortis") in the first clause where the Hebrew has "Sheol."
notes.13:15: Vulgate "dividet" ("will divide") reflects a Hebrew root meaning "separate," whereas the Masoretic Text reads a wordplay on Ephraim's name ("will flourish/bear fruit").
notes.14:1: Following the Hebrew versification, chapter 14 begins here (in the other common versification this verse is 13:16 and 14:2-10 are 14:1-9); Vulgate "Pereat" ("May [Samaria] perish") and "ad amaritudinem concitavit" ("provoked to bitterness") also differ from the Masoretic Text ("shall bear her guilt ... rebelled").
notes.14:3: Vulgate "vitulos labiorum nostrorum" ("the calves of our lips") follows the Hebrew wording, whereas the Septuagint reads "the fruit of our lips."
notes.14:4: Vulgate "Dii nostri opera manuum nostrarum" forms a plural nominal clause without a preposition before "works," and "ejus, qui in te est, misereberis pupilli" makes God the active subject ("You will have mercy on the orphan who is in You"), differing slightly from the Masoretic Text ("for in You the orphan finds mercy").
notes.14:5: Vulgate "contritiones" ("bruises" or "crushings," matching the Septuagint) contrasts with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "their apostasy" or "backsliding."
notes.14:9: In the Vulgate punctuation, "Ephraim, quid mihi ultra idola?" is spoken by God to Ephraim, and the accusative "ut abietem virentem" ("like a green fir tree") modifies Ephraim ("eum") rather than God as in the Masoretic Text ("I am like a luxuriant cypress").
